scope: Six newly verified pre-registered sources for fusion, reranking, routing and diagnostic evaluation. Two additional returned sources were already verified in earlier batches and were not counted again.

verified_claims: Elasticsearch RRF combines results from two or more child retrievers.
rank_constant defaults to 60 and must be at least 1; larger values give lower-ranked results more influence.
rank_window_size defaults to 10, must cover the request size, and increasing it can improve relevance at additional performance cost; filters can apply to child retrievers.
records.boundary: These defaults and constraints are Elasticsearch implementation behavior, not universal RRF defaults. Quality and cost depend on child retrievers, filters and candidate windows.

verified_claims: The v2 rerank endpoint accepts a query and document list and returns ordered results with relevance scores.
The documentation recommends at most about 1,000 documents per request; top_n limits returned results and long documents are truncated to max_tokens_per_doc, default 4096.
Scores are normalized to [0,1] but are ranking signals rather than linear probabilities or cross-request comparable quantities.
records.boundary: Truncation can remove evidence and API limits, model behavior and errors affect production use. Score thresholds require task-specific calibration.

verified_claims: The paper studies near-OOD intent detection for unseen intents within a known domain without fine-tuning.
It evaluates multiple prompting methods and several LLMs on public and internal datasets, and studies the effect of the number of in-distribution intents.
It proposes a hybrid approach combining a small classifier's ID capability with LLM OOD generalization for cost and robustness.
records.boundary: Near-OOD is not arbitrary domain shift. Internal datasets, model versions and prompts limit reproducibility; the abstract does not establish a universal rejection threshold or production error rate.

verified_claims: RAGRouter-Bench evaluates adaptive RAG routing using canonical query types and fine-grained corpus structural and semantic indicators.
The benchmark jointly measures generation quality and resource consumption across multiple RAG paradigms and backbone LLMs.
Its experiments report no one-size-fits-all paradigm and a better effectiveness-efficiency trade-off for adaptive routing in the benchmark.
records.boundary: Results depend on constructed query-corpus pairs, paradigms, backbones and LLM-as-a-Judge; they do not define a universal routing policy or deployment threshold.

verified_claims: The study compares No Context, Gold Context and training-free Iterative RAG on ChemKGMultiHopQA with an evidence-aware controller alternating retrieval and hypothesis refinement.
It diagnoses hop coverage, query quality, composition fidelity and stopping calibration, and reports up to 25.6 percentage-point improvement over Gold Context in its setting.
Staged retrieval can reduce late-hop failure and context overload, while incomplete hop coverage, distractor latch, premature stopping and composition failure remain.
records.boundary: The result is specific to scientific multi-hop QA, the dataset and controller, and cannot be generalized as a production RAG gain or perfect-answer guarantee.

verified_claims: MMR combines query relevance with novelty or dissimilarity to selected documents to reduce redundancy during reranking or passage selection.
Lambda equal to 1 approximates relevance-only ranking while lambda equal to 0 favors diversity.
The early TIPSTER experiments report preliminary benefits for ad-hoc retrieval and especially non-redundant multi-document summarization.
records.boundary: These are early experiments with task-specific similarity and lambda settings. Diversity can trade off narrow-topic precision and is not a general quality guarantee.
